protocol_name: iPSC to microglia-like cells, end to end on chip

sizing.capsule_count_note: not in chip spec; sheet default 100,000 used

events.narration: Fill the expansion chamber with coating solution so the iPSCs have a surface to attach to. FILL: 1.0 chamber volume(s) to put the reagent in, not a sweep to get the old liquid out; about 37% of what was there stays behind.
Hold the coating in place at 37 C, then it is displaced by the first medium change.
Load iPSCs into the expansion chamber. Flow stops so they can settle.
No flow for 24 hours while the cells attach. Oxygen comes from the recirculating reservoir, not from fresh medium.

Daily feed on day -6: iPSCs get a full daily change, so this one is meant to clear the spent medium out rather than top it up. SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Grow on through day -6.

SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Grow on through day -5.

SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Grow on through day -4.

SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).

SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Grow on through day -2.

Lift the iPSCs as small aggregates with an enzyme-free reagent. Aggregates, not single cells, are what the next stage needs. FILL: 1.0 chamber volume(s) to put the reagent in, not a sweep to get the old liquid out; about 37% of what was there stays behind.
Carry the aggregates downstream into the hemogenic chamber. This replaces a pipette transfer between flasks.
No flow for 24 hours while the aggregates attach and spread. The run stops here if the day-0 colony count is out of range.

Day 0: change into mesoderm medium. A stage switch has to clear what was there, or the previous stage's medium keeps driving the cells, so this one sweeps. Imaging has counted the colonies and confirmed the seeding density is in range. SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Days 0 to 2: mesoderm specification.

Day 2: half exchange, leaving half the conditioned medium behind. The cells depend on their own secreted factors, so this is never a full change. PARTIAL change: 0.5 of a chamber volume. This is NOT trying to clear the chamber - the conditioned medium left behind is wanted, as in any bench half-change.
Day 2 to 3.

Day 3: change into hematopoietic medium, which starts the switch from mesoderm to hemogenic endothelium. Another stage switch, so it sweeps rather than half-changes. SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Growing on to day 5. From about day 7 the first progenitors round up and lift off the endothelial layer.

Day 5: half exchange. Spent medium leaves through the waste port and is kept as a supernatant sample. PARTIAL change: 0.5 of a chamber volume. This is NOT trying to clear the chamber - the conditioned medium left behind is wanted, as in any bench half-change.
Growing on to day 7. From about day 7 the first progenitors round up and lift off the endothelial layer.

Day 7: half exchange. Spent medium leaves through the waste port and is kept as a supernatant sample. PARTIAL change: 0.5 of a chamber volume. This is NOT trying to clear the chamber - the conditioned medium left behind is wanted, as in any bench half-change.
Growing on to day 9. From about day 7 the first progenitors round up and lift off the endothelial layer.

Day 9: half exchange. Spent medium leaves through the waste port and is kept as a supernatant sample. PARTIAL change: 0.5 of a chamber volume. This is NOT trying to clear the chamber - the conditioned medium left behind is wanted, as in any bench half-change.
Day 9 to 10: progenitors keep accumulating above the adherent layer.
Harvest 1, day 10: carry the floating progenitors downstream. The adherent layer stays put, so it keeps producing.

Bring the progenitors down the line from the hemogenic chamber and concentrate them here, which replaces a centrifugation step. Cells left upstream are cells lost, so this is sized to clear the chamber it sweeps, not to top it up. The depth weir leaves a 25 um gap under the lid, so it holds back capsules and aggregates of roughly 75 um and above. It does NOT retain bare cells of 10-15 um: see protocols/retention_audit.md. SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Distribute the progenitors across the four maturation chambers.
Day 10 to 12: the endothelium produces a second batch.
Harvest 2, day 12: carry the floating progenitors downstream. The adherent layer stays put, so it keeps producing.

Bring the progenitors down the line from the hemogenic chamber and concentrate them here, which replaces a centrifugation step. Cells left upstream are cells lost, so this is sized to clear the chamber it sweeps, not to top it up. The depth weir leaves a 25 um gap under the lid, so it holds back capsules and aggregates of roughly 75 um and above. It does NOT retain bare cells of 10-15 um: see protocols/retention_audit.md. SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Distribute the progenitors across the four maturation chambers.
Progenitors settle and begin to adhere in maturation medium. Flow stays off while they attach.

Day 40: bring the cells from all four maturation chambers together in the harvest module.
Cool to 4 C before dissociation. Cold handling limits the activation that warm enzymatic lifting causes in this cell type.
Fill with a gentle, enzyme-free dissociation reagent. FILL: 1.0 chamber volume(s) to put the reagent in, not a sweep to get the old liquid out; about 37% of what was there stays behind.
Hold cold while the cells release from the surface.

Quench with a carrier-protein buffer so the released cells do not stick to the channel walls. FILL: 1.0 chamber volume(s) to put the reagent in, not a sweep to get the old liquid out; about 37% of what was there stays behind.

Wash out the dissociation reagent, with the suspension passing over the depth weir. Reagent carried into the encapsulation chip keeps working on the cells, so this one has to clear. The depth weir leaves a 25 um gap under the lid, so it holds back capsules and aggregates of roughly 75 um and above. It does NOT retain bare cells of 10-15 um: see protocols/retention_audit.md. SWEEP: 4.6 chamber volumes in total, which is what the 99% exchange goal needs in a well-mixed chamber (what is left after V chamber volumes is exp(-V), so half a volume cannot clear it however often it is repeated).
Deliver a counted, filtered single-cell suspension to the outlet, ready for the encapsulation chip.
